title: Pluggable delivery policies
idea: An extensible event bus takes its retry rules as a `RetryPolicy` strategy, adds behaviour by wrapping subscribers in decorators, and builds validated settings with a builder.
points: `RetryPolicy` answers two questions: how many attempts, and how long to wait.
A decorator implements `Subscriber` and wraps another, adding dedupe or metrics.
Decorator order matters: the outer one sees every call first.
A builder holds defaults and refuses invalid settings before the bus runs.

hero.title: Where new features go

left.title: Edit the bus each time
items: Dedupe adds a flag and a branch inside deliver
Each new backoff adds another case in the bus
Every change retests the whole delivery loop

right.title: Plug in at the seams
items: A new RetryPolicy class leaves the bus untouched
Subscriber decorators add dedupe, metrics or logging
The builder sets defaults and rejects bad settings

hero.verdict: The delivery loop is written once. New behaviour arrives as new classes.

code.title: Strategy, decorators, builder
code.caption: The core loop never changes. Backoff, dedupe and counting are all added as separate classes.

walk.text: The builder sets exponential backoff and remembers the last 1000 ids; print the delays.
Wrap billing in two decorators: count outside, skip duplicates inside.
Deliver EV-1 twice and EV-2 once; EV-2 fails twice before it succeeds.
The core loop asks the policy for attempts and delays. It never changes.
RetryPolicy is the strategy; FixedDelay and ExponentialBackoff plug into it.
Deduplicating marks an id only after success, so a failure is still retried.
The builder holds defaults and rejects invalid values before any bus sees them.

pitfalls: Mark an event as seen only after the handler succeeds, or failures are lost.
Cap exponential delays; add random jitter, seeded only in tests, so retries spread out.
Bound the dedup memory; an unbounded set of ids grows forever.

quiz.q: What does the waited line print?
quiz.why: Counting is outside, so the duplicate EV-1 still counts as a call. EV-2 fails twice, giving two backoff waits of 100 and 200 ms.

takeaway: Strategies for policy, decorators for behaviour, a builder for settings.

starters: Why should Counting wrap Deduplicating and not the other way round?
